newsitem.title: USA: Perry defends extra U.S. Bosnia force in Senate.
newsitem.headline: Perry defends extra U.S. Bosnia force in Senate.

text.p: Defense Secretary William Perry said on Thursday the U.S. peacekeeping force in Bosnia would leave in December as promised and a new 5,000-member covering force was not a way to send U.S. troops back there.

Responding to sharp Republican questioning about the role of the covering force, Perry told the Senate Armed Services Committee he had made no recommendation to President Bill Clinton on whether a new NATO peacekeeping force would be needed in Bosnia after the current one leaves this year.

"The IFOR mission is over and it will be withdrawn when its mandate ends on December 20," Perry said, referring to the 60,000-strong NATO force sent to Bosnia to oversee implementation of the peace accords signed last December.

Perry and General John Shalikashvili, chairman of the joint chiefs of staff, told the senators that the new force of 5,000 Americans going to Bosnia from Germany would be there only to cover the peacekeepers' withdrawal.

But Republican senators said the plan to keep the new covering force in Bosnia until March did not square with repeated Clinton administration commitments to have U.S. troops out of Bosnia by the end of the year.
"The credibility gap between you and Congress is as wide as the Grand Canyon," said Senator John McCain, an Arizona Republican and a strong critic of administration policy on Bosnia.
